newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian troops in riot drill ahead of election.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian troops in riot drill ahead of election.

text.p: "Protesters" hurled projectiles at troops, a phalanx of riot police advanced ahead of armoured cars, sirens blared and cars and tires were set ablaze in Indonesia's capital on Thursday.

But the projecticles were water-filled plastic bags and the confrontations between the troops and demonstrators were good-natured as riot police took part in a training exercise ahead of possibly more serious protests in the run-up to next year's parliamentary elections.

The exercise, held on a major thoroughfare in the Kemayoran district near the site of Jakarta's old airport, involved more than 500 security personnel in uniform and scores of their colleagues masquerading as demonstrators.

The demonstrators, some wearing red bandanas, carried placards and banners which read "Increase the minimum wage" and "The thoughts of the people should not be asleep" as they jostled with the troops and police in full riot gear.
Sirens blared from helicopters which circled the scene and armoured cars throughout the 90-minute exercise as senior military and government officials watched from a nearby overpass.
Fire brigade and para-medical personnel were also involved in the exercise.
There have been two major political protests in Jakarta this year, both linked to the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), whose official colours are red and black.
Members of the party clashed with riot police on June 20 as a government-backed PDI faction held a meeting to oust party head Megawati Sukarnoputri.
On July 27, police raided the PDI headquarters to oust Megawati's supporters from the building. The raid led to the city's worst rioting in more than 20 years in which at least five people died.

Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, is not contesting the parliamentary elections, scheduled for May-June next year. The government has not recognised her faction of the PDI as one of the parties permitted to contest elections.

The ruling Golkar party, the government-backed faction of the PDI and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only groups allowed to nominate candidates for the 425 elected seats in parliament.
